headline: New law requires sanctions and tariffs tied to Russia, extends Iran sanctions through 2031, and expands a teacher tax deduction to early childhood educators.
what_it_does: The law requires the President to block visas and property of certain people, including the Russian president and some Russian military commanders. It requires tariffs of up to 100% on all goods from any of the five largest buyers of Russian oil or gas if that country knowingly makes new purchases. It bans sending US energy products to Russia, bars Americans from new investments in Russia or buying Russian government debt, and bans trading shares of Russian government-linked companies on US stock exchanges. It also extends the Iran Sanctions Act of 1996 through 2031 and lets early childhood educators claim the federal tax deduction for teacher expenses.

who_it_affects.group: Russian officials and military commanders named in the law
who_it_affects.how: They face blocked property in the US and denial of US visas.

who_it_affects.group: US importers and shoppers buying goods from major buyers of Russian oil or gas
who_it_affects.how: Goods from those countries could face tariffs of up to 100% of their value if the countries keep making new purchases.
They may not export, reexport, or transfer US energy products to or within Russia.
They are barred from making new investments in Russia, buying Russian government debt, or trading shares of Russian government-linked companies on US exchanges.

who_it_affects.group: Companies doing business with Iran's energy sector or weapons programs
who_it_affects.how: They remain subject to required US sanctions, now extended through 2031.

who_it_affects.group: Early childhood educators, such as preschool and childcare workers serving children under 6
who_it_affects.how: They become eligible for the federal tax deduction for certain out-of-pocket educator expenses.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted September 18, 2026; the summary does not give specific start dates for each part, though the tariff applies to new purchases made after enactment and the Iran sanctions extension runs through 2031.
